copy.hero_headline: The Bay is the fastest lane your team isn't using.
copy.hero_sub: A commuter water network for Bay Area employers — electric hydrofoil vessels, terminal-to-terminal, faster than the bridge at rush hour.
copy.stripe_lesson: In 2024 we ran the first employer water commute on the Bay — daily service for Stripe employees, North Bay to Oyster Point. The ride delivered: smooth, quiet, four feet above the chop, a desk on the water. Two things didn't, and we're saying so plainly. First, we flew an eight-seat executive vessel on a mass-commute job — the economics of a commuter line need our twenty-seat vessel, built for exactly this. Second, we secured docks ahead of demand instead of demand ahead of docks — this time, employer letters of intent come first, and they are what unlock the berths. The ride worked. The structure is what we fixed.
copy.loi_cta: We are sequencing the first commuter lines now. A letter of intent is non-binding — it costs nothing and commits nothing. It tells us which line to light up first, and it gives us the demand evidence that unlocks terminal access. Option A: reserve seats for your team on a line. Option B: anchor a line — underwrite the vessel, brand the service, own the schedule.
copy.price_anchor: roughly a parking space — often less
